Minimum geometric coverage required by the shape check. Lines are compared in both directions, so extra ink and missing reference segments reduce the score. This is geometric similarity, not recognition confidence.\n\nHigher values are stricter. At 73%, a score of 72% fails. Stroke count, required hooks, dictionary rules and correction limits must also pass.

Maximum distance from a reference line at which a point still counts as matching. Measured as a percentage of the larger glyph dimension and used to calculate shape coverage.\n\nAt 5%, a deviation of up to 5% of that dimension is allowed. Higher values make line comparison more forgiving. This does not move the drawing or change the minimum coverage threshold.

Maximum whole-glyph shift allowed to align with the reference. The limit applies separately to horizontal and vertical movement, as a percentage of the input field.\n\nAt 12%, each axis may shift by up to 12% of the field. Higher values allow more displacement. 0 disables translation correction. The total budget also limits the correction used. Original ink is preserved.

Allowed uniform enlargement or reduction of the entire drawing. Width and height change by the same factor, measured relative to the original drawn size.\n\n30% permits scaling to 70–130% of the original size. Higher values allow larger size corrections. 0 disables this correction. X and Y controls adjust proportions separately; the total budget still applies.

Additional width correction after uniform scaling. This percentage allows a narrow or wide glyph to be corrected without changing its height by the same factor.\n\n15% permits an X factor from 0.85 to 1.15. Higher values allow larger proportion changes. 0 disables only X correction; Y remains independent. The total budget applies.

Additional height correction after uniform scaling. This percentage allows a short or tall glyph to be corrected without changing its width by the same factor.\n\n15% permits a Y factor from 0.85 to 1.15. Higher values allow larger proportion changes. 0 disables only Y correction; X remains independent. The total budget applies.

Maximum whole-drawing rotation in degrees for alignment with the reference, clockwise or counterclockwise.\n\n8° allows up to 8° in either direction. Higher values allow more rotated glyphs; 0 disables rotation correction. This does not check the direction of pen movement along a stroke. Budget cost depends on how far the rotation moves points.

Allowed horizontal shear correction in degrees: parts at different heights move horizontally by different amounts. This corrects an italic-like slant, unlike rotating the entire glyph.\n\nHigher values allow stronger shear. 0 disables it. The correction counts toward the total budget; original strokes are preserved.

Maximum deviation permitted when simplifying small hand tremors. Measured as a percentage of the larger drawn glyph dimension, adjustable in 0.1% steps.\n\nHigher values can remove more small bends. 0 disables simplification. Stroke endpoints are preserved, and strokes with required hooks are protected. Removing points also consumes the total budget and does not change saved ink.

Limits the combined amount of shape correction. Each correction costs its maximum point displacement as a percentage of the larger reference dimension; these costs are added. Smoothing uses the distance of removed points to the retained line.\n\nThis is not a sum of degrees or slider values. Higher budgets allow more combined correction. Costs of 10% and 8% total 18%. 0 removes only the combined limit; individual correction limits still apply.

Checks whether the Japanese language model recognizes the handwritten glyph as the requested kanji. Its first candidate must match exactly; the expected answer is not supplied as a hint.\n\nRecognition runs on device after downloading the model. Without it, enabling is unavailable: download it in general Settings first. Geometric sliders do not tune this model. Ignore excludes readability from the final check.

Compares drawing geometry with the reference: line coverage, stroke count, required hooks and enabled dictionary features. Allowed corrections may be applied within their limits and budget.\n\nStroke order and drawing direction are checked separately. Coverage, correction, budget and dictionary controls apply to shape. Ignore excludes this check from the final result.

Checks stroke sequence and the direction of movement along each stroke against the reference. Stroke count must also match. Order and direction are enabled together.\n\nThis is independent of readability and shape; geometric correction sliders do not tune it. Ignore excludes order and direction from the final check.

Additional rules for a specific kanji: which strokes cross, which end against another stroke and which of two strokes must be shorter. Only relations listed in the dictionary for that glyph are checked.\n\nIgnore disables these rules and hides their tolerances. Stroke count and required hooks are still checked. A dictionary rule may override the general tolerance below. This setting belongs to the shape check.

Minimum difference when the dictionary requires one stroke to be shorter than another. Measured relative to the longer stroke, using each full stroke path length.\n\nAt 5%, the short stroke must be at least 5% shorter. Higher values are stricter. At 0, it must still be strictly shorter; equality fails. A rule-specific value overrides this setting.

Maximum gap between a stroke endpoint and another stroke that still counts as touching. Measured as a percentage of normalized glyph size.\n\nHigher values accept larger gaps; lower values require closer joins. 0 removes the gap allowance without disabling the rule. Applies only to dictionary relations; a touching rule may supply its own tolerance.

Minimum continuation past an intersection needed to count as a crossing rather than an endpoint touching another stroke. Length is measured along the line as a percentage of normalized glyph size.\n\nHigher values require more pronounced continuation and affect the crossing-versus-touching distinction. 0 does not disable rules. A crossing rule may supply its own tolerance.
